fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Algebraic Semantics and Categorical Characterization of Program Logics

fr:mainmatter.fr:p: There is a duality between categorical constructs and logical systems. For propositional logic, the Stone duality states an isomorphism between presentations of Boolean algebras (quotients of the free Boolean algebra of a given signature) and logical systems in that signature. For Hoare and separation logics, however, there is no such categorical account. What should such an account look like?

Fuckyou, I am a researcher in program semantics and verification.
This blog documents my scientific ideas in various topics.

A general theme is to provide unifying semantic guarantees for probabilistic programs and their associated logics. This is an ambitious project spanning different levels of abstraction. At the bottom, we have probability theory and many theorems are proven by classical analysis. This is particularly un-suitable for formal reasoning. Hence, one goal is to find a layer of axioms that separates the formal reasoning about programs and the underlying analysis obligations. I conjecture this can be done with new categorical foundations, such as Markov, QBS, Integrable Cones, Finite Valuation Approximable domains.

Next, suppose we have a good logic to reason with probabilistic programs and have implemented it. We should seek to write different statistical techniques in a programming model, so that our logic can soundly reason with their denotations. The logic can also be directly deployed to reason with programs.

Next, suppose we have a program describing some machine learning system component. Very likely, there are floating point operations in that program. Practical computers provide only an approximation to idealized operational and denotational semantics, which are formulated in ideal real numbers. Does there exist a set of rules which allows us to reason with such approximation compositionally? What are the compromises? ...
I hope to answer as many of these questions as possible in the next 3 years.
